title: Finite certificate schema verifier
label: prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier
statement: For every load-bearing manuscript claim $c$ whose component kinds lie in the seven-kind domain, $V(c,\mathcal C)$ is a finite, prose-insensitive record-schema verifier for the declared publication certificate. If $V$ accepts, then $\mathcal C(c)$ is locally checkable at exactly its declared evidence level. This is certificate-record verification only: it checks finite record shape, dispatch, evidence pointers, and command-boundary discipline, not end-to-end external semantic validation of the referenced artifacts or source theory. If $V$ rejects, then a reviewer can extract a finite bad subrecord consisting of the first failed schema check and the fields on which that check depends.
proof_start: The verifier inspects only the displayed tuple $\mathcal C(c)$, the finite seven-kind domain, the finite dispatch table $\Gamma$, and the finite list of paths, rows, commits, or logs cited by the record. Since $K$ is required to be a subset of the seven-kind domain, the set \(\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)\) is finite. The checks over $E$, $R$, and the command-run fields are therefore finite lookups in named manuscript or bundle surfaces, not semantic judgments about generated prose. title: Finite certificate obstruction skeleton
label: thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton
statement: Let $c$ be a load-bearing manuscript claim whose component kinds lie in the seven-kind domain. The verifier of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier} gives the following complete audit classification at the declared evidence level. A certificate for $c$ passes the publication-safety interface if and only if it has no bad subrecord of the following five types: \begin{enumerate} \item missing evidence surface for the declared evidence level; \item missing pass record for a gate in $\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$; \item missing human-promotion record when the claim crosses from intake or source material into active publication work; \item discovery escalation without the pinned discovery-gate source-interface rows for certificate, ledger, lineage, and boundary witnesses; or \item command-run escalation without command, source commit, environment, exit code, and log path. \end{enumerate} Equivalently, every unsafe accepted claim contains an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord of one of these five types, and deleting all other fields preserves the same rejection by the verifier. This is an audit-skeleton theorem for the software-workshop route: it classifies finite certificate failures and makes no claim about theorem-proving complexity or about fresh execution of the underlying workflow.
proof_start: Let $K$ be the finite set of component kinds of $c$. Since $K$ is a subset of the seven-kind domain, Proposition~\ref{prop:claim-kind-dispatch} gives a unique finite required gate set \[ G(c)=\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k). \] The certificate field $R$ is indexed by exactly this finite set, so checking gate passage is a finite lookup: each $g\in G(c)$ must have a pass record and the record must cite an item of the finite evidence surface $E$. Overlap asks whether the route duplicates or conflicts with a sibling route; its evidence is route identity, overlap ledgers, submitted-sibling paths, and board state. title: Scheduler selection is advisory before discovery gating
label: prop:scheduler-selection-advisory
statement: Let $s$ be a scheduler or critical-path score attached to a candidate claim $c$. If $s$ recommends selecting $c$, then the recommendation is a work-selection claim and by itself can only pass the scheduler gate. If $c$ is also asserted to be a discovery or classifier-shifting contribution in a gate-sound pipeline, then the accepted mixed claim must pass both the scheduler gate and the discovery gate. Consequently, critical-path scores may prioritize review order, and the imported classifier-shift selection rule may break ties among otherwise equal discovery potential coordinates, but neither score nor recommendation accepts a classifier-shift discovery unless the discovery gate also supplies the required certificate, ledger, and lineage witnesses.
proof_start: By the definition of $\Gamma$, a scheduler recommendation has claim kind work-selection, so its atomic gate is the scheduler gate. The scheduler gate's evidence surface records a score, backlog window, or analogous critical-path priority; none of these fields is a semantic naming certificate, a ledger witness, a DNA-complete theorem genome, a score certificate for a discovery claim, a lineage witness, or a not-claimed boundary. title: Conditional publication safety interface
label: thm:publication-safety-interface
statement: Consider a theory-to-paper pipeline with the operational interface above. Assume that every load-bearing claim in an active manuscript is either rejected or has an acceptance entry with an evidence surface; that the pipeline is gate-sound for acceptance; that every advisory output is demoted unless the deterministic gate set $\Gamma$ for its claim kind passes; that discovery claims are checked through the pinned discovery-gate interface certified by Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and Propositions~\ref{prop:reviewable-source-snapshot-interface} and \ref{prop:source-interface-record-file-consistency}, in particular its pipeline safety and main pipeline theorem labels; and that no inactive intake seed is treated as publication work without human promotion. Then, conditional on those workflow assumptions, any accepted load-bearing claim in the manuscript admits a locally checkable publication certificate $\mathcal C(c)$ accepted by the finite schema verifier of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}. Consequently the claim has a recorded evidence surface, a declared evidence boundary, and a prior pass record for every gate required for its claim kind. Moreover, accepted discovery claims inherit the bounded pinned source-interface consequences that statement-only, code-only, mechanical-expansion, and compression-only outputs are not accepted as discovery without the required certificate, ledger, and lineage witnesses. Any purported accepted claim without such finite certificate data is rejected by one of the five obstruction skeletons in Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}. This theorem is a conditional safety interface: it does not independently prove that an arbitrary implementation is gate-sound, that all gates were run, or that path-verified rows are command-run evidence.

Gate-soundness supplies the pass-record field $R$ for every gate assigned by $\Gamma$. title: Gate-witness criterion
label: lem:gate-witness-criterion
statement: A case record is a path-verified witness for the safety interface when it names the source or artifact surface, the invariant that failed, the gate decision, and the safe manuscript lesson. Under Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, such a witness can support a case-study claim, but not a stronger command-run claim, unless the corresponding command log is also recorded.
proof_start: The four named fields are exactly the data required by the definition of a path-verified evidence level: they identify where the case is checked, which gate predicate is being evaluated, what decision was made, and which bounded claim may be carried into the manuscript. The definition of command-run evidence has additional required fields: command, source commit, environment, exit code, and log path. Therefore a witness record with only the four path-verified fields supports the bounded case-study claim and cannot be used as evidence for a fresh command-run assertion.\qed

title: Evidence-level overclaim obstruction
label: thm:evidence-level-overclaim-obstruction
statement: Fix the certificate schema, dispatch function, and evidence-level vocabulary of this paper. Let $c$ be a load-bearing claim whose accepted certificate has level path-verified and whose boundary field $B$ records that no command-run assertion is made. Then every stronger reading of $c$ that asserts any of the following additional conclusions is rejected by the finite schema verifier: \begin{enumerate} \item external gate soundness for an arbitrary implementation of the workflow; \item Lean correctness, full-source rebuild success, or axiom-purity beyond the recorded formal-source gate fields; \item end-to-end external semantic validity of artifact data beyond the finite manifest and evaluator surfaces named in $E$ and $R$; \item a fresh daemon run, full-source rerun, Rule110 or GroundCompiler rerun, or journal or workshop acceptance; or \item bundle-backed reviewability when neither \path{review_bundle/} nor an archival equivalent carrying the same finite records is in the submitted artifact boundary. \end{enumerate} More precisely, such a stronger reading has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord of one of the five types in Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}. Hence the accepted claim is rigid at its declared evidence level: path-verified certificate records cannot be promoted by prose into command-run evidence, semantic validation, formal-source correctness, or external acceptance.
proof_start: Let $c^+$ be one of the stronger readings. It has the same displayed manuscript sentence as $c$ but a larger claim-kind set, a stronger evidence level, or a larger submitted-artifact boundary requirement. The verifier does not inspect rhetorical emphasis; by Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier} it inspects only the finite tuple $\mathcal C=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ and the finite dispatch table.
